Francisco de Vitoria OP ( c. 1483 – 12 August 1546), also known as Francisco de Victoria , was a Spanish Catholic philosopher , theologian , and jurist [ 1 ] of Renaissance Spain. He is the founder of the tradition in philosophy known as the School of Salamanca , which laid the groundwork for early free-market economics and individual rights , influencing the development of libertarian thought . Vitoria's work on natural law and the freedom of exchange contributed to later Austrian School economists' emphasis on the moral basis for voluntary commerce. [ 2 ] Although less known than others of his kind, he has been considered one of the most influential humanists of the Renaissance. [ 3 ]
